newsitem.title: USA: Northrop files $750 million suit. [CORRECTED 23:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Northrop files $750 million suit. [CORRECTED 23:56 GMT]

text.p: Defense giant Northrop Grumman Corp Monday filed a $750 million lawsuit against the U.S. government seeking to recover losses it incurred on an Air Force missile contract.
(Company corrects suit amount to $750 million from $756 million)

In a statement, the company said the government did not make a program risk assessment and report to Congress on the AGM-137 Tri-Service Standoff Attack Missile (TSSAM) program in accordance with applicable federal procurement statutes and regulations, thus voiding the fixed-price contract. The company said it is seeking to recover its uncompensated performance costs, investments and a "reasonable profit."
Northrop said it had completed about 75 percent of the engineering, manufacturing and development and nearly 50 percent of the flight testing when the cancellation occurred in 1995.
The missile was designed for Air Force, Navy and Army conventional precision strike missions.
